command.try: Try the draft on its bench
command.openStarter: Open a starter project in VS Code
config.url: Address of the Picodev CTF (https only; http for localhost and 127.0.0.1). A machine setting: an open folder cannot change it. The author token, VS Code's sign-in and, for a password-protected site, its password are kept per address in VS Code's secret storage.
view.author: Author
welcome.game.noPicodev:
Next: start a game. This window has no picodev command: it comes with a challenge's container, where you build and send your program.
[Start a game](command:picodevCtf.launch)
[Open a starter project](command:picodevCtf.openStarter)
welcome.game.none:
Next: join a game. Start it on the site with "use my machine", then enter the 8-character code its screen shows.
[Join a game](command:picodevCtf.login)
[Start a game](command:picodevCtf.launch)
welcome.game.pending:
Next: join the game. A code came from the game screen; it is kept 15 minutes in this window's memory only.
[Join](command:picodevCtf.joinPending)
welcome.game.pendingStarter:
Next: open the starter project in its container. A code came from the game screen (kept 15 minutes in this window's memory only); join from the container's window, where picodev is.
[Open the starter project](command:picodevCtf.openStarter)
[Join](command:picodevCtf.joinPending)
welcome.courses:
Next: read a course. The courses of the catalogue show here; sign VS Code in on the site to keep your progress.
[Open a course](command:picodevCtf.openCourse)
[Sign in](command:picodevCtf.signIn)
[Browse the courses on the site](command:picodevCtf.courses)
welcome.author:
Next: set your author token. Writing a challenge needs the author role and a ctfa_… token, made in your profile on the site.
[Set the author token](command:picodevCtf.setToken)
[picodev.fr](https://picodev.fr)
walkthrough.play.title: Play a challenge from VS Code
walkthrough.play.description: From the catalogue to the flag: your machine, the challenge's container, the game's bench.
walkthrough.docker.title: Docker and Dev Containers
walkthrough.docker.description:
A challenge is played in its family's container: install Docker and the Dev Containers extension. Nothing else to install: the compilers and picodev come with the container.
[Install Dev Containers](command:workbench.extensions.search?%22ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers%22)
walkthrough.docker.alt: Before playing: install Docker, then the Dev Containers extension (Install, in the Extensions view).
walkthrough.launch.title: Start a game
walkthrough.launch.description:
Pick a challenge in the catalogue. VS Code signed in, in a challenge's container: confirm, and the game opens and is joined from here, the Regarder page beside. Otherwise it opens on the site, where you start the game with "use my machine" (credits and payment stay on the site).
[Start a game](command:picodevCtf.launch)
walkthrough.launch.alt: In the Picodev CTF view, Actions: click Start a game, pick a challenge, then on the site choose On your machine and open the game.
walkthrough.open.title: Open the project in its container
walkthrough.open.description:
"Back to VS Code" on the game screen brings the game code here. Open the starter project of the challenge's family in its container, then join the game.
[Open a starter project](command:picodevCtf.openStarter)
[Join a game](command:picodevCtf.login)
walkthrough.open.alt: On the game screen, click Back to VS Code; in the notification, Open the starter project; in its container, join the game.
walkthrough.build.title: Build and send
walkthrough.build.description:
Build in the container (errors go to the Problems panel), then send the program to your game's bench.
[Build](command:picodevCtf.build)
[Send to the bench](command:picodevCtf.playerSend)
walkthrough.build.alt: In Actions, click Build, then Send to the bench: the program runs on the game's bench.
walkthrough.console.title: Board console
walkthrough.console.description:
Follow what the board does on the bench (serial output, pins) in a terminal of its own.
[Board console](command:picodevCtf.console)
walkthrough.console.alt: In Actions, click Board console: a terminal shows the board's serial output and pins.
walkthrough.flag.title: Hand in the flag on the game screen
walkthrough.flag.description:
The flag is handed in on the game screen, never from the extension. Hints and abandon are there too.
[Game screen](command:picodevCtf.gameScreen)
walkthrough.flag.alt: In Actions, click Game screen; on the game screen, paste the flag and submit it.
